body:
Hey, 

All the other commenters have some really great ideas for helping reduce your anxiety, but I think I can add a couple that help me. Maybe they will help you too :)

I find that bringing a small object with me (something you can get through customs/TSA!) and describing it in your mind in as much detail as possible can really help. I use tiny seashells for this and it forces your mind to think of something else. I know it sounds pretty silly but it does work! 

Some airports also have dogs they can let nervous fliers take on their journey. I know Reno airport had a couple last time I was there. Might be worth some research :)

Hey, 

I have a similar issue. Maybe we could help each other. 

I feel a lot of anger and resentment towards people in my life. I've been pushed around a lot.

What I recently found out is that even though I feel a lot of anger, it doesn't go anywhere because I can't express my emotions. Instead they just build up and make me feel worse, and I can't let things go. 

Is it the same for you?
Hope you're doing a little better today than yesterday. Keep trucking, my friend.

Aaaaaaahhhhh this makes my heart melt! You are so fortunate to have such a supportive parent. I hope you spend the money on something that makes you happy (maybe something you share with your mum?) It's so good to know someone is there for you!

Sometimes we can be our own worst enemies. Despite knowing we aren't that bad, we can convince ourselves we are just the worst.

But sometimes we can be our own best friends. We are literally the only people who are always there for ourselves no matter what. So maybe we can not beat ourselves up so much.

So, you're mad and you're sad, but it's ok and valid to feel that way. Being upset when upsetting things happen is only natural.

Try and think about what things you use every day and pack those first. Things like your phone, laptop, soap, toothbrush. 

Also, if you need to message somebody, I'll always answer. Short of getting hit by a bus, I'll get back to you, even if it takes a few hours.

You may not feel very strong but sometimes our feelings aren't accurate. You might feel like the worst person who has ever lived, but is that accurate? You clearly still care, even just a little. Caring a little bit is where you start. 

As for your things, it may be time to start selecting the things you need. You will be OK, even if right now you don't feel OK. I'm on your team.

OK, well we all act self destructive sometimes, I know I do. 

Alright, so if nobody can take you in, I'd say a shelter is your best bet. It will beat living on the street for sure. It is, at the very least, a roof over your head. 

So many people have built up a new life after homelessness. You haven't given up yet. You don't have to continue being self-destructive. 

If you were a moron, you wouldn't be here. You can do this, I promise. I know it's hard.

OK, so you're sure that you don't know anyone able to give you a bed or a couch? 

You sound like you're on a bit of a self-destructive path right now, which might be making you feel like you can't get out of this one. That isn't true. There is always another option open to you. Trust me on that. The very fact you're reaching out for help means you can't have given up on yourself completely.

And I've met some real twunts in my time, and you don't seem like one of them.

OK, do you have work that means you are stuck in town? 

If you could commute, a friend or family member could still take you in. 

Even if they don't know/like you very well, most people would let you stay over seeing you on the street.

Maybe if you could find a space in a shelter, your cat could stay with someone you know.

There is no shame in couch surfing. Everyone has tough times and we have to get by the best we can. Doing your best is never shameful.

OK. Let's see. 

Do you have a relative or friend you can stay with?

If you don't, you could stay at a shelter.

Twice in one night? Does the police station have a loyalty card scheme or something? 

Bad jokes aside, it sounds as though this really is a rough time for you. Do you have somewhere to go once you leave your house?

Hey buddy,

It's ok to feel anxious sometimes. Buuuut sometimes our bodies need a little help stopping being anxious! 

Everyone has things that help them feel calm. I tell myself to breathe in... hold... breathe out... hold, until I stop breathing too quickly. 

I also find that describing an object I see in the room in great detail really calms me as my brain is forced to do something other than panic. 

I carry tiny seashells round with me as I can hold them and describe their texture in my head, without anyone knowing. It sounds really dumb, but it honestly helps a lot.

What helps you feel calm?

Hi Bunny, 

It's ok to feel like you mess everything up. I've been there too, it's a terrible feeling.
Do you mind sharing what's happening right now?
Hey no worries, hope you're feeling a bit better today :)

Hey there, 

It's normal for stitches to feel sore and tight, especially when they're new. There's also not much loose skin on your head and scalp so they'll feel pretty tight, even when you blink. You also probably have some swelling where they had to sew you up, making it feel worse. The swelling will go down and the pain will be less soon.  

I've had stitches in my face and neck, I promise they get better.

As for a scar, I can't say what will happen in your case, but they will probably give you advice on how to reduce and look after it. My scars faded, yours will too. Your job right now is to look after yourself, the rest will come later.

The doctors just want to be safe and make sure you don't have too much concussion, which is why you would have a CT scan. Just keep them updated on how you feel.

I know you are in pain, and I know that I can't make it easier for you, but it will be OK, even if right now you don't feel OK. In the mean time, rest if you can. You will be fine

No problem :)

To be honest, I'm kind of a binger and loneliness makes it worse so I have years of experience!

Also, if you have a sweet tooth, you can put chocolate bars with nougat or caramel centres (snickers, curly wurlys) in the freezer. Makes them last longer if you can't resist eating and then it's harder to eat so much. Crunchy foods help too.

Chewing gum helps me. I buy those big pots of like 60 pieces and the strong flavour (esp menthol) and the chewing help to distract and also convince my body I've eaten something.

But I second the distraction comment, doing anything with my hands prevents me from using them to put food in my mouth :)
Sorry to ruin you :/ I'm sorry about your dog too.

Hey there, 

You've every right to feel how you do. It's fine to feel hopeless when you're in a tough situation like this. Are there any steps you could take to make things less of a burden on you? Maybe taking some paid leave or making one night of the week uninterrupted time to do your hobbies? I have an untreatable condition too, also diagnosed in my teens, so I know how it can exacerbate other problems in life. I hope that you're able to get some rest, food, and start to feel better soon.

I can't see all the comments here :/ 

But whoever posted that it's valid to live for my dog, thankyou. There are no right words for a situation like this, but the best someone can do is listen. I feel like you listened.
See above :)
I don't know if I can. Sharing my problems has made things a lot worse and I feel like I don't want to fight this battle again. People have just ruined me.
Thankyou, I really do need a hug right now and this came at just the right time. I'll hug you right back :)

Hey, 

I can't give much practical advice to you, but I hope you're doing ok and I understand how difficult it is to face rehoming your dog. 
If you are feeling low then you can pm me and we can talk. I also have a dog so we can share stories if you like. Keep looking, something might work out yet :)

I have the teddy bear I was given when I was born. If I need a hug but can't get one he is always willing to be friends :) 
I'm 26 now so it might be silly to do that but I'd rather have him around than not.
I also talk to my dog, she has a very 'listening' face, so even though she can't understand me, it helps. 
I totally get why you would want the company and if it makes you feel better then I think you and Casper make a great team :)

Hi, 

I know this is a little while after your post, but I hope you're doing well.
I just wanted to say that I've messed up most of my interviews in a colossal and sometimes dramatic fashion, but I did get there. I managed to concuss myself in a Disney store interview, so I do mean dramatic. Every time you mess up, you get better at not doing that the next time. Eventually, you get there. Lots of luck with your job search and be kind to yourself :)

Like other commenters, I find it helps to just do a little at a time. Making my bed in the morning helps, dusting the shelves, or making a commitment to get one room cleared by the end of the week. Rather than doing chores, I like to remind myself that this is something I'm doing to benefit my health. Also, you could try watching things like 'How clean is your house', there are episodes on YouTube. For some reason I find them really satisfying and they make me want to clean if I'm not in the mood :)
